concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish land-building endogenic forces from land-wearing exogenic forces and explain why relief persists.
Define a geomorphic agent and distinguish it from a geomorphic process.
Explain why gravity and gradients are essential for all surface movement of earth materials.
Identify the sources of energy that drive endogenic processes.
Describe orogenic, epeirogenic, earthquake and plate tectonic processes under diastrophism.
Explain what volcanism includes as an endogenic process.
Explain how solar energy, gravity and stresses drive exogenic processes.
State the processes included under denudation.
Analyse how climate and rock type and structure control rates of exogenic processes.

topics.title: Weathering
topics.ncert_sections: Weathering; Chemical, Physical and Biological Weathering; Special Effects; Significance

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish chemical, physical and biological weathering processes.
Explain exfoliation as a result of unloading and thermal expansion.
Evaluate the role of weathering in soils, erosion, biodiversity and ore enrichment.
Explain why mass movements are gravity-driven and not a form of erosion.
Identify the activating causes and favourable conditions for mass movements.
Distinguish slump, debris slide, debris fall, rockslide and rock fall.
Explain erosion and compare climatically and non-climatically controlled agents.
Explain deposition as a consequence of loss of energy of erosional agents.

topics.title: Soil formation
topics.ncert_sections: Soil Formation; Process of Soil Formation; Soil-forming Factors

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the stages of soil formation from the weathering mantle to mature soil.
Explain the role of parent material, topography and time as passive soil-forming factors.
Explain how climate and biological activity act as active soil-forming factors.
